# BPMN 2.0 element support

What the Sutra engine actually executes, generated from the `Node` enum in
[`src/model.rs`](src/model.rs) and the loader's reject arm in [`src/loader.rs`](src/loader.rs).
Three exhaustive `match`es make this page un-driftable: a new node kind does not compile
until it is described here.

This is the ONLY BPMN implementation. Nothing downstream forks it, extends it or
overrides it: a distribution adds codecs, transports, redactors and validators through
the SPI crates, never a node type, a gateway, or an execution semantic. So "which BPMN
features does <that repo> have?" needs no investigation — read this page. (Whether a
given checkout is at the same REVISION of the crate is a separate question, and a real
one: the trees are synced by copying, not by git.)

The **wait state** column is the load-bearing one: a process containing any node that
parks is stateful, and is ineligible for `execute_sync`. `inherited` means the node
parks iff its inner/wrapped flow does.

## Supported flow nodes

| BPMN 2.0 XML | `Node` variant | Wait state | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<startEvent>` (± `<timerEventDefinition>`) | `StartEvent` | no | The process entry point. Triggered EITHER by an inbound message on one of its `<q:source channel>` channels OR by a timer schedule — never both; a start declaring both trigger contracts is rejected at load. A timer start arms a durable schedule row at activation and fires with EMPTY variables. |
| `<endEvent>` | `EndEvent` | no | Ends this token's path; other live tokens keep running. |
| `<endEvent>` + `<terminateEventDefinition>` | `TerminateEndEvent` | no | Ends the whole instance, not just this token. |
| `<endEvent>` + `<errorEventDefinition>` | `ErrorEvent` | no | Throws a BPMN error for a boundary / event sub-process to catch. An empty code means "any error". |
| `<endEvent>` + `<cancelEventDefinition>` | `CancelEndEvent` | no | Valid only inside a `<transaction>` — rolls its store transaction back. |
| `<intermediateThrowEvent>` | `IntermediateThrowEvent` | no | Emit-and-continue. `ThrowKind` selects the flavour: none, compensate, message, signal, escalation, link. A message throw requires `<q:send>`. |
| `<intermediateCatchEvent>` + `<linkEventDefinition>` | `LinkCatchEvent` | no | The synchronous goto target of a link throw — a jump, not a park. Each link name must have exactly one catch. |
| `<intermediateCatchEvent>` + `<messageEventDefinition>` | `MessageCatchEvent` | **yes** | Parks until a correlated inbound arrives on one of its channels. Correlation is by `<q:alias>`. |
| `<intermediateCatchEvent>` + `<timerEventDefinition>` | `TimerCatchEvent` | **yes** | Parks a durable TIMER `waiting_event` row due at the resolved instant. `<timeDuration>` and `<timeDate>` only — `<timeCycle>` is rejected here (a token cannot park at a node that fires repeatedly). |
| `<boundaryEvent>` | `BoundaryEvent` | no | Attached to an activity. `BoundaryKind`: Error, Compensation, Escalation, Cancel, Timer. A timer boundary needs a wait-capable host (channel-call serviceTask / userTask) — it fires when the host's park outlives the duration. `@cancelActivity="false"` makes it non-interrupting. |
| `<serviceTask implementation="…">` | `ServiceTask` | **when** `@implementation` starts with `channel:` | Routed on `@implementation` by task-kind precedence. A `channel:`-prefixed implementation is a channel call: it parks until the correlated response (or its `<q:timeout>` boundary). Anything else is a registered task or a template, and runs inline. |
| `<serviceTask>` with data associations, no `@implementation` | `DataTask` | no | Declarative: its store reads, FEEL assignments and store writes ARE its behaviour. No registered task is resolved. |
| `<scriptTask>` + `<script>` | `ScriptTask` | no | `<bpmn:script>` names a file in the module's `scripts/` folder (SRL). |
| `<manualTask>` | `ManualTask` | no | A pure no-op pass-through — a modelling marker, not a wait state. |
| `<sendTask>` | `SendTask` | no | Emit-and-continue; its `<q:send>` is required (enforced at load). |
| `<businessRuleTask>` | `BusinessRuleTask` | no | Evaluates a DMN decision file and merges the result into the variables. |
| `<userTask>` | `UserTask` | **yes** | Parks until an external relay resumes the instance on one of its channels. |
| `<callActivity>` | `CallActivity` | no | Invokes another process by `@calledElement` (optionally cross-module via a namespace). Data associations on the call itself are rejected — pass data through the called process's declared variables. |
| `<subProcess>` | `SubProcess` | inherited | Embedded: expanded inline and run synchronously by the inline runner. See "Scope constraints" — the inline runners cannot park mid-scope. |
| `<transaction>` | `TransactionSubProcess` | inherited | One store transaction around the inner flow; a `<cancelEventDefinition>` end rolls it back. |
| `<adHocSubProcess>` | `AdHocSubProcess` | no | Activities with no enforced sequence flow, run in document order until a FEEL `<completionCondition>` holds. |
| `<subProcess triggeredByEvent="true">` | `EventSubProcess` | no | ERROR-TRIGGERED ONLY. Fires when an error escapes an activity in its enclosing scope and no boundary event catches it. Message/timer/signal triggers are rejected — those are wait states, so model them on the stateful surface instead. |
| `<exclusiveGateway>` | `ExclusiveGateway` | no | XOR. At most one outgoing flow fires, chosen by FEEL condition in document order, with `@default` as the fallback. |
| `<inclusiveGateway>` | `InclusiveGateway` | no | OR-fork / OR-join. |
| `<parallelGateway>` | `ParallelGateway` | no | AND-fork / AND-join. |
| `<complexGateway>` | `ComplexGateway` | no | Inclusive-style fork plus a FEEL `<activationCondition>` N-of-M join. |
| `<multiInstanceLoopCharacteristics>` (marker on an activity) | `MultiInstance` | inherited | Wraps the inner activity. Sequential or parallel, driven by `<loopCardinality>` or a `loopDataInputRef` collection, with an optional FEEL `<completionCondition>`. |
| `<standardLoopCharacteristics>` (marker on an activity) | `StandardLoop` | inherited | Wraps the inner activity. Test-before (while) or test-after (repeat) on a FEEL `<loopCondition>`, bounded by `@loopMaximum`. |

## Rejected flow nodes

The loader fails closed on these rather than ignoring them — diagnostic `SUTRA.CONFIG.BPMN.UNSUPPORTED_ELEMENT`.

| BPMN 2.0 XML | Model it instead as |
|---|---|
| `<task>` | An abstract task has no behaviour to execute — pick a concrete task type. |
| `<receiveTask>` | Use `<intermediateCatchEvent>` + `<messageEventDefinition>`, or a `<userTask>`. |
| `<eventBasedGateway>` | Racing wait states are not modelled; park on one catch event. |
| `<implicitThrowEvent>` | Use `<intermediateThrowEvent>`. |
| `<event>` | The abstract base element is not a concrete flow node. |

## Accepted but inert

| BPMN 2.0 XML | Why it carries no token |
|---|---|
| `<dataObject>` / `<dataObjectReference>` | Modelling-only; process data lives in `<q:variables>`. |
| `<dataStore>` / `<dataStoreReference>` | Not a flow node, but `<dataStoreReference>` DOES carry `<q:store>`, which binds it to a durable key in a data store. |
| `<laneSet>` / `<lane>`, artifacts, `<documentation>` | Inert process children. |

## Scope constraints

The inline sub-process runners cannot park a durable wait state mid-scope, so the loader
rejects a durable park nested inside one:

| Rejected combination | Diagnostic |
|---|---|
| A channel-call `<serviceTask>` or an `<intermediateCatchEvent>` timer inside `<subProcess>`, `<transaction>`, `<adHocSubProcess>` or an event sub-process | `SUTRA.DISPATCH.TIMER.UNSUPPORTED` |
| `<q:retry>` on any node inside one of those sub-processes (a retry park is a durable timer) | `SUTRA.CONFIG.BPMN.RETRY_NOT_APPLICABLE` |
| An event sub-process whose start event is not error-triggered | `SUTRA.PARSE.SUBPROCESS.UNSUPPORTED` |
| An `<intermediateCatchEvent>` with an event definition other than message / timer / link | `SUTRA.PARSE.BPMN.UNSUPPORTED_CATCH_EVENT` |

Model the parking node at the top level of the process instead.

## The `q:` extension surface

Node types are only half the model; the `q:` namespace (`urn:sutra:q:1.0`) carries the
message binding, correlation, retry, store and audit contracts. `xsd/q.xsd` is
authoritative for its exact shape — read it, not a design doc, when you need the
attributes an element supports.
